correctness.rationale: Ground hub; rim Dirichlet Laplacian is A=3I−S−S^-1. Periodization of r^|j|/√5 and the explicitly derived squared-Green kernel gives exact c_d and u_d. Rank-one/rank-two Woodbury on the zero-sum subspace yields S=Nσ/α, D=2N[ασ+c_d(u_d−1/N)]/(α²−c_d²), I=2Nc_dY_d/[α(α²−c_d²)]; connection guarantees α>c_d>0. Strict decrease and discrete convexity of the positive infinite-line kernels establish decrease of c_d,u_d and Y_d through half the cycle; adjacent interaction is positive, hence unique maximum at d=1 and at most one interaction sign change. Explicit n=3..7 boundary algebra, and majorant B_4=125000000000/152387956161<1 decreasing for m≥4, prove the n=6 threshold. Uniform r^d(d/5+O(1))−1/N asymptotics for d=O(log n) give the claimed first-negative scale. Independent fresh numerical Laplacian direct inverses agreed at all 599 separations for 3≤n≤49. These finite checks are not the all-n proof.

value.rationale: A sharp optimized perturbation theorem for the natural Kirchhoff index of a common network family. The competition of superadditive near spoke losses and subadditive distant losses is described quantitatively at all graph sizes, including an exact n=6 onset and a nontrivial log-log separation scale.

final_claim: For unit wheel W_n with n rim vertices, deleting adjacent spokes uniquely maximizes the Kirchhoff-index damage over spoke pairs; two-spoke interaction has at most one sign transition in separation, is negative for a sufficiently wide pair iff n≥6, and the first negative separation k_n=(log n+log log n)/log((3+√5)/2)+O(1). Exact rank-two Green formulas determine all finite n.
limitations: No claims for weighted wheels, rim-edge failures, or more than two spoke failures.
Some finite direct inverse calculations use floating arithmetic, while analytic inequalities and exact boundary certificate establish unrestricted results.
